glossary.Oxygen saturation: The percentage of haemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry.
glossary.SpO2: Oxygen saturation measured by a finger pulse oximeter.
glossary.Opioid overdose: Taking too much of an opioid drug such as heroin or morphine, depressing breathing.
glossary.Opioid: A drug like morphine, heroin or codeine acting on opioid receptors to relieve pain.
glossary.ET tube: Endotracheal tube: a tube passed through the mouth into the trachea to ventilate the lungs.
glossary.Intubation: Passing a tube into the trachea to secure the airway.
glossary.Oesophagus: The food pipe from throat to stomach.
glossary.Trachea: The windpipe carrying air to the lungs.
glossary.Air entry: Breath sounds heard with a stethoscope, showing air is reaching that part of the lung.
glossary.Lung bases: The bottom parts of the lungs.
glossary.Distended abdomen: A swollen, bloated tummy; here from air pumped into the stomach.
glossary.Foreign body: An object that should not be there, such as food or a toy in the airway.
glossary.CNS depression: Reduced activity of the brain and spinal cord, slowing breathing and consciousness.
glossary.Sedatives: Drugs that calm and make drowsy, such as benzodiazepines.
glossary.Respiratory failure: Lungs unable to keep blood oxygen up or carbon dioxide down.
glossary.COPD exacerbation: A flare of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with worse breathlessness and cough.
glossary.Brainstem stroke: A stroke in the brainstem, which contains the breathing centres.
glossary.Anaesthesia: Drug-induced loss of sensation or consciousness for procedures.
glossary.Gastric reflux: Stomach contents coming back up the oesophagus.
glossary.Non-fasted: Has eaten recently, so the stomach is full and aspiration risk is high.
glossary.Ventilation: Moving air in and out of the lungs.
glossary.Imaging: Scans such as X-ray or CT.
glossary.Airway adjunct: A device that helps keep the airway open, such as an oropharyngeal airway.
glossary.Mouth-to-mask: Rescue breaths given through a pocket mask over the patient's mouth and nose.
glossary.Smooth muscle tone: The background tension in muscle that keeps the airway open.
glossary.Agonism: A drug binding to and switching on a receptor.
glossary.Brainstem respiratory centres: Areas in the medulla and pons that set the rate and depth of breathing.
glossary.Ventilatory response: The body breathing harder in response to a rise in carbon dioxide.
glossary.Pharyngeal: Relating to the pharynx, the throat behind the mouth and nose.
glossary.Laryngeal: Relating to the larynx, the voice box.
glossary.PaO2: Partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood.
glossary.PaCO2: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in arterial blood.
glossary.ROSC: Return of spontaneous circulation: the heart beating on its own again.
glossary.Resuscitation: Emergency treatment to restore breathing and circulation.
glossary.Altered GCS: A drop in consciousness level on the Glasgow Coma Scale.
